name: dkj-solutions
displayName: Claude Specialists - DKJ policy for DKJ-Solutions (policy scaffold, DKJ-Solutions scope)
description: DKJ-Solutions' codex: the binding rules every DKJ-Solutions app shares, packaged so they are written once instead of rebuilt per repo. The counterpart of bwj-development for the other organisation, and an ADDITIVE add-on to dkj-policy that contradicts nothing it decides. Two chapters. THE HOUSE STYLE: one set of design tokens, twelve themes a user picks from (six light, six dark) and one base stylesheet for every page, report, dashboard or Artifact a DKJ-Solutions app renders. The canonical files live in this plugin's assets/house-style folder; the house-style skill points there and carries the rules a session needs before it fetches them. A repo adds its own domain tokens and components on top and never redefines a house token, and the CHECK-HOUSE-STYLE gate holds it to that: every vendored copy is the pinned one, no house token or class is redefined, no retired token name is used -- run as a CI gate through a reusable workflow, and read-only at session start by its own SessionStart hook, HOUSE-STYLE-SESSIONCHECK. THE TRACKER LABELS: a feat/ pull request and a feature issue carry feature, a fix carries bug. Its second SessionStart hook is DEV-PREVIEW: a repo whose scripts/repo-config.ps1 states Get-DevPreview (the command, the port or port range, the URL path) gets its local dev server started or reused at session start and its localhost link handed to the owner and the session, and beside it the plugin's own general pages server (Artifacts, Issues, Release notes, SessionStart) is started on ports 4890-4899; a repo that states nothing pays nothing. Carries no specialists. Requires dkj-subagents-alpha and dkj-policy. Enable this in DKJ-Solutions repos only -- never in BWJ-Development, which has its own styling.
